name: stri_trim
title: Trim Characters from the Left and/or Right Side of a String

origin.description: Trim preserved-class boundaries from one or both sides.
origin.usage: stri_trim(str, side = c("both", "left", "right"), pattern = "\\P{Wspace}", negate = FALSE)

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: Character vector of strings to trim.

arguments.name: side
arguments.text: both, left, or right. A unique prefix is enough. NULL uses both.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Class of code points to preserve, unless negate is TRUE. The default preserves non-whitespace.

arguments.name: negate
arguments.text: If TRUE, the pattern is the class to trim rather than the class to preserve.

origin.details: pattern names the code points to preserve when negate is FALSE, and the code points to trim when negate is TRUE. The default \P{Wspace} preserves every non-whitespace code point, so whitespace is trimmed. \p{Z} does not include tab. Trimming removes only a leading or trailing run; characters between the first and last preserved code point stay. stri_trim, stri_trim_both, stri_trim_left, and stri_trim_right are separate functions. side uses match.arg.
origin.example:
x <- stri_trim("  a  ")
sentence <- paste0('stri_trim("  a  ") returns ', x, '.')
writeLines(sentence)

translation.description: Trim preserved-class boundaries from one or both sides.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: String, missing value, or list of those.

arguments.name: side
arguments.text: both, left, or right. A unique prefix is enough. None uses both.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Class of code points to preserve, unless negate is true. The default preserves non-whitespace.

arguments.name: negate
arguments.text: If true, the pattern is the class to trim rather than the class to preserve.

translation.details: pattern names the code points to preserve when negate is false, and the code points to trim when negate is true. The default \P{Wspace} preserves every non-whitespace code point, so whitespace is trimmed. \p{Z} does not include tab. Trimming removes only a leading or trailing run; characters between the first and last preserved code point stay. stri_trim, stri_trim_both, stri_trim_left, and stri_trim_right are separate functions. side uses the same unique-prefix rule as match.arg.
translation.value: A list of strings. A missing result is NA.
translation.example:
from stringi.charclass import stri_trim
x = stri_trim("  a  ")
sentence = f'stri_trim("  a  ") returns {x[0]}.'
print(sentence)
